newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe tightens exchange controls on stocks.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe tightens exchange controls on stocks.

text.p: Zimbabwe's central bank on Wednesday reintroduced exchange controls on the transfer of dual quoted shares from a foreign market to the Zimbabwean register.
The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe said in a statement it had become necessary for exchange control to look at all cases involving transfers of shares from a foreign to the local register.
It did not elaborate and bank officials were unavailable for further comment.
"With immediate effect, specific applications must be submitted to exchange control for the transfer of dual quoted shares to the Zimbabwean register," it said.

Stock market brokers, describing the measure as retrogressive, said it was likely to affect liquidity in such dual-listed counters as hotel and supermarket group Meikles, merchant banker National Merchant Bank and regional conglomerate TZI TZI.ZI.
"It's a retrogressive measure in terms of liberalisation policies," one broker said.
"Knowing the Reserve Bank, it will probably take three to four weeks to get foreign exchange approval and in the meantime share prices on the markets would be changing," another one said.

The central bank lifted in January exchange controls on the transfer of a dual-quoted shares from a foreign to the local market but limited foreign participation in the dual-listed company to a total of 40 percent for both the local and foreign registers.
